feature: Pin an actual island organism, compare inherited variation, and find matching or contrasting marker genotypes
changes: Pin the selected actual organism as reference A using ephemeral component state; choose another recorded organism as B through the existing native controls.
A and B show actual organism IDs, species, birth generations and birth islands, inherited trait copies, their arithmetic averages, and neutral-marker genotypes.
Only distinct organisms of the same species receive a numeric B-minus-A difference, expressed as inherited trait index points on the 0–100 display scale.

Find same or different marker genotypes among actual members of the displayed island and generation using the pinned species. Counts exclude reference A; buttons are disabled when no eligible members exist.

Repeated search clicks scan the entire cohort in recorded order after the selected ID and wrap deterministically. Searches select real organisms through the existing view controls without adding saved state or drawing random numbers.
Reference A remains available across islands, recorded generations, settings changes and normal advancement. A replacement expedition suppresses the old pin immediately and clears its state.

Inspect pinned organism visits its actual birth generation, island and species while selecting its exact ID, then scrolls and focuses the existing full inspector; clear remains available when selection is empty or a different species.
Native pin, inspect and clear controls support keyboard use and the non-WebGL fallback; compact comparison cards stack on phones.
scientificCorrectness: The comparison displays two organisms’ recorded inherited copies; it does not imply genes changed within an individual.
Trait-copy equality treats the two copies as unordered and uses unrounded recorded values. Equal trait averages can result from different copy pairs.
A/a and a/A are the same unordered neutral-marker genotype. The marker is inherited separately and one marker does not estimate genome-wide diversity.
Genotype search names its exact island, generation and species. Its caption explicitly describes deliberately found examples, not random samples or an explanation of an evolutionary cause.
The numeric index difference alone does not explain a population’s evolution or rank breeding success.
Actual birth records supply identity and origin context. Pinning, browsing, clearing and inspecting change presentation state without drawing model random numbers.

validation.scope: These results cover only the logged focused unit suites, two selected EvoLab golden checks, and the eleven browser journeys listed below. They do not claim a full repository test run.

focused.execution: The existing 26 unit checks across the three listed suites and six fresh comparison/search edge cases ran in separate logs. Counts are parsed from completed Vitest summaries and checked against the expected scope.

render.scope: Two selected EvoLab golden checks; the skipped count is recorded from the filtered render run.

browser.scope: Two new resident comparison journeys, two existing field-card journeys, three existing archipelago journeys, and four existing island-framing journeys. All eleven have successful result lines; each spec explicitly disables retries.

translationDelta.baselineScope: The finalizer captures current read-only hashes and verifies its artifact writes leave both shared catalogs unchanged; this is not a claim about unrelated collaborators’ edits.

validation.priorValidationReportScope: All existing validation JSONs, including resident-comparison-pending-validation.json, are excluded from the finalizer outputs and checked for unchanged bytes across finalization.
